expectations.text: Flags the GitHub token (ghp_...) found in commit 111aaa as a high-severity finding, even though scripts/deploy.sh was deleted entirely in a later commit
expectations.evidence: 'Finding 1 — HIGH severity ... GitHub personal access token (ghp_ prefix) ... Introduced Commit 111aaa22'.

expectations.text: States that the finding exists only in git history now (the file was deleted, not just edited) and is still recoverable via git
expectations.evidence: 'In current working tree? No — file deleted. In git history? Yes — both commits contain the value.'

expectations.text: Masks the GitHub token value in the report (e.g. ghp_1A2B****Yz12), never printing it in full
expectations.evidence: Masked value ghp_****Yz12; the literal never appears.

expectations.text: Remediation explicitly says to revoke/rotate the GitHub token via GitHub, says that deleting the file in commit 222bbb is not remediation, and recommends git filter-repo (or BFG) rather than git rebase -i or git commit --amend to purge it
expectations.evidence: 'Rotate immediately: GitHub -> Settings -> Developer settings'; 'Deleting the file does not purge the secret'; filter-repo prescribed with an explicit warning against rebase -i and commit --amend.

expectations.text: Does not flag 'your-token-here' in scripts/README.md as a confirmed/high-severity leaked credential — recognizes it as an obvious placeholder rather than a real secret
expectations.evidence: 'scripts/README.md — Clean. Contains only the placeholder string ... This is not a credential.'

expectations.text: Does not report the `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN` header line as a separate secret finding — it is a shell variable reference, not a literal credential — restraint / false-positive check
expectations.evidence: The Bearer header line is never reported as a finding.
